speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. Since you mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to understand the specifics of your symptoms and surgical history. Can you describe exactly when the pain occurs and how the earrings cause discomfort?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you describe as "shooting when eating" suggests referred pain from the auriculotemporal nerve. Has this sensation radiated specifically to your jaw or temple, and does your jaw click or lock when you open your mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia secondary to post-tympanoplasty adhesions or nerve compression.
